DataFormatSpecifications.label: BAR
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: BAR is a binary data format specification created by Affymetrix where the data is stored in big-endian format. The format of the file is a header section followed by sequences sections (one section per sequence defined). The BAR file contains one and two sample analysis results (signal and p-values) from the tiling array software.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: BPMAP
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: BPMAP is a binary data format specification created by Affymetrix where the data is stored in big-endian format. The BPMAP format contains information relating to the design of the Affymetrix tiling arrays.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CDF binary format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The CDF binary format is a binary data format specification created by Affymetrix was created for faster access and smaller file size in comparison to the CDF ASCII format. The values in the file are stored in little-endian format. CDF binary format describes the layout for an Affymetrix GeneChip array. An array may contain Expression, Genotyping, CustomSeq, Copy Number and/or Tag probe sets. All probe set names within an array are unique. Multiple copies of a probe set may exist on a single array as long as each copy has a unique name.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: It is unclear whether, originally, this format was intended to be the ASCII or binary version of the CDF format. As such, this class has been renamed as the binary format, and a new class created (CDF ASCII format) to make both options available.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CEL binary format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: CEL binary format is a binary data format specification created by Affymetrix where values are stored in little-endian format. The CEL format stores the results of the intensity calculations on the pixel values of the DAT file. This includes an intensity value, standard deviation of the intensity, the number of pixels used to calculate the intensity value, a flag to indicate an outlier as calculated by the algorithm and a user defined flag indicating the feature should be excluded from future analysis. The file stores the previously stated data for each feature on the probe array.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: It is unclear whether, originally, this format was intended to be the ASCII or binary version of the CEL format. As such, this class has been renamed as the binary format, and a new class created (CEL ASCII format) to make both options available. (22/05/2013)

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CHP binary format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: CHP binary format is a binary data format specification created by Affymetrix, stored in little-endian format and used to store expression, resequencing and genotyping results from algorithms implemented in the GCOS 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4 and BRLMM Analysis Tool software applications.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: As this is a child of Binary format, it is assumed that this class is intended to represent the binary form of this format. As described in the definition sources, there are other formats for CHP available.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: pdf
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: PDF is an open standard for document exchange.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: PostScript
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: PostScript is a format used for describing documents.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: tex
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: tex is a format for documents written in the document markup language and document preparation system LaTeX.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: genomedata format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Genomedata provides a way to store and access large-scale functional genomics data in a format which is both space-efficient and allows efficient random-access. Genomedata archives are implemented as one or more HDF5 files, either as single files or as directory archives. HDF5 archives are self describing, like XML, but may also contain more complex structures such contain binary data.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: DWG
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: DWG ("drawing") is a binary file format used for storing two and three dimensional design data and metadata

DataFormatSpecifications.label: DXF
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: DXF (Drawing Interchange Format, or Drawing Exchange Format) is a CAD data file format developed by Autodesk for enabling data interoperability between AutoCAD and other programs.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: raster image format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A raster image is a format for representing a rectangular grid of dots (pixels) which contains information on the specific colour of each pixel.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: BMP
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The BMP File Format is a Raster graphics image file format used to store bitmap digital images, independently of the display device (such as a graphics adapter).

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CGM
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Computer Graphics Metafile (CGM) is a free and open international standard file format for 2D vector graphics, raster graphics, and text, and is defined by ISO/IEC 8632.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: GIF
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The Graphics Interchange Format (GIF) is a bitmap image format. The format supports up to 8 bits per pixel thus allowing a single image to reference a palette of up to 256 distinct colors. The colors are chosen from the 24-bit RGB color space. It also supports animations and allows a separate palette of 256 colors for each frame. The color limitation makes the GIF format unsuitable for reproducing color photographs and other images with continuous color, but it is well-suited for simpler images such as graphics or logos with solid areas of color. [wikipedia]

DataFormatSpecifications.label: JPEG
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: JPEG is a lossy file format for storing images

DataFormatSpecifications.label: JPEG 2000
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: JPEG 2000 is a compression standard enabling both lossless and lossy storage. The compression methods used are different from the ones in standard JFIF/JPEG; they improve quality and compression ratios, but also require more computational power to process. [wikipedia]

DataFormatSpecifications.label: PNG
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: PNG is a bitmapped image format and video codec that employs lossless data compression.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: TIFF
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: TIFF is a flexible, adaptable file format for handling images and data within a single file, by including the header tags (size, definition, image-data arrangement, applied image compression) defining the image's geometry.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: vector image format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A vector image is a collection of connected lines and curves that produce objects. This geometric description enables the image to be displayed without loss at any size rendering.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: outline document format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A format specification for data used or produced by outliner software

DataFormatSpecifications.label: OmniOutline format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A proprietary format for documents created and edited using OmniOutliner outliner software,

DataFormatSpecifications.label: OPML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: OPML (Outline Processor Markup Language) is an XML format for outlines

DataFormatSpecifications.label: .class file
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A format in which a .java file has been compiled into bytecode using a Java compiler and which is specified to be executed using the Java virtual machine.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: .java file
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A source code file format which is specified to be used with the Java programming language.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: RDF
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The Resource Description Framework (RDF) is a general-purpose language for representing information in the Web.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: Data in RDF format can be serialised into XML, textual, or binary format.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: RDF-XML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A serialisation of RDF into an XML format.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: BioPAX RDF/XML format
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: AL 6.9.22: I would prefer to use the updated RO label 'has characteristic', but for some reason Protege only allows the use of the label RO deems older, 'bearer of'

DataFormatSpecifications.label: tabix file format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Tabix indexes a TAB-delimited genome position file and creates an index file when region is absent from the command-line. The input data file must be position sorted and compressed by bgzip which has a gzip like interface. After indexing, tabix is able to quickly retrieve data lines overlapping regions specified in the format "chr:beginPos-endPos". Fast data retrieval also works over network if URI is given as a file name and in this case the index file will be downloaded if it is not present locally.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: spreadsheet format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A spreadsheet data format is one in which data is organised into a matrix (or matrices) of columns and rows to form cells in which values are entered.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: WKn
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: WKn is a collective name for a spreadsheet format created for Lotus 1-2-3.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: Please note that this is a collective class for all versions of the WKn format, and the specific version required should be created as necessary and placed as a child of this class.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: XLS spreadsheet
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A spreadsheet data format designed for Microsoft Excel.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: XML spreadsheet
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A spreadsheet data format in which the structure of the data is described using XML, such as column and row headers and cell identity.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: BedGraph
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The bedGraph format is a line-oriented text file format. Bedgraph data are preceeded by a track definition line, which adds a number of options for controlling the default display of this track. Following the track definition line are the track data in four column BED format. The bedGraph format allows display of continuous-valued data in track format. This display type is useful for probability scores and transcriptome data. This track type is similar to the wiggle (WIG) format, but unlike the wiggle format, data exported in the bedGraph format are preserved in their original state.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: cls
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Categorical (e.g tumor vs normal) class file format

DataFormatSpecifications.label: OBO Flat File Format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: OBO format is the text file format used by OBO-Edit, the open source, platform-independent application for viewing and editing ontologies.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CDF ASCII format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The CDF ASCII format is an ASCII data format specification created by Affymetrix similar to the Windows INI format. This format describes the layout for an Affymetrix GeneChip array. An array may contain Expression, Genotyping, CustomSeq, Copy Number and/or Tag probe sets. All probe set names within an array are unique. Multiple copies of a probe set may exist on a single array as long as each copy has a unique name.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: CEL ASCII format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: CEL ASCII format is ASCII data format specification created by Affymetrix similar to the Windows INI format. The CEL format stores the results of the intensity calculations on the pixel values of the DAT file. This includes an intensity value, standard deviation of the intensity, the number of pixels used to calculate the intensity value, a flag to indicate an outlier as calculated by the algorithm and a user defined flag indicating the feature should be excluded from future analysis. The file stores the previously stated data for each feature on the probe array.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: Data File Standard for Flow Cytometry
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The flow cytometry data file standard provides the specifications needed to completely describe flow cytometry data sets within the confines of the file containing the experimental data. The principal goal of the Standard is to provide a uniform file format allowing files created by one type of acquisition hardware and software to be analyzed by another type.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: FCS3.0
DataFormatSpecifications.parent: Data File Standard for Flow Cytometry
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: FCS3.0 is version 3.0 of the Data File Standard for Flow Cytometry. It contains a mechanism for handling data sets of 100 megabytes and larger, support for UNICODE text for keyword values, support for cyclic redundancy check (CRC) validation for each data set, a requirement for the inclusion of information describing the method of signal amplification and increased support for the inclusion of time as a measurement parameter.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: tab delimited file format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Tab delimited file format is a plain text file format where each field value of a record is separated from the next by a tab stop character.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: gct
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Gene Cluster Text file format

DataFormatSpecifications.label: MAGE-TAB
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: MAGE-TAB is a tab delimited data format comprimising of ADF file for array design, IDFfor experimental design, SDRF for sample data relationships and associated data files.
DataFormatSpecifications.comment: A simple spreadsheet-based, MIAME-supportive format for microarray data: MAGE-TAB.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: SIF
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: SIF stands for Simple Interaction Format, and is a text format invented for Cytoscape. If the file contains any tab characters, then tabs are used to delimit the fields and spaces are considered part of the name. If the file contains no tabs, then any spaces are delimiters that separate names (and names cannot contain spaces).

DataFormatSpecifications.label: HTML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: html, or HyperText Markup Language in full, is a data format specification is a markup language for web pages and is the publishing language of the World Wide Web.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: Microsoft Word doc
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: A file format for word processing documents for Microsoft Word.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: XML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Extensible Markup Language (XML) is a standard set of rules for encoding documents in a machine-readable form defined by the W3C.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: FieldML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: FieldML is an XML-based language for describing time-varying and spatially-varying fields. The aims of the language design process are to keep the language concise, consistent, intuitive and flexible.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: GML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: GML stands for Graph Markup Language, and is a standard network file format; supported by multiple generic network software packages

The PSI-MI format is an acronym for the Proteomics Standards Initiative - Molecular Interaction format. It provides an XML standard for molecular interactions and is supported by many molecular interaction databases and tools.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: MathML 2.0
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: MathML 2.0 is an XML format which is a low-level specification for describing mathematics as a basis for machine to machine communication. It is a W3C Recommendation and was released on 21 Feb 2001. A product of the W3C Math working group, it provides a much needed foundation for the inclusion of mathematical expressions in Web pages.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: OWL-XML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: The Web Ontology Language (OWL) in XML serialization

DataFormatSpecifications.label: OWL2-XML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Web Ontology Language version 2 in XML Serialization

DataFormatSpecifications.label: SBML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML) is a machine-readable format for representing models. It's oriented towards describing systems where biological entities are involved in, and modified by, processes that occur over time.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: Taverna workflow format
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: Format of Taverna workflows.

DataFormatSpecifications.label: XGMML
DataFormatSpecifications.definition: XGMML stands for eXtensible Graph Markup and Modelling Language, and it is a XML standard; similar to but preferred over GML.

OperatingSystems.label: Mac OS
OperatingSystems.definition: Mac OS is software which is used as the operating system for the Macintosh personal computer created by Apple Inc.

OperatingSystems.label: OS X
OperatingSystems.definition: OS X is a Mac OS operating system which succeeds the original Mac OS, which had been Apple's primary operating system since 1984. Unlike the earlier Macintosh operating system, OS X is a Unix-based operating system.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: application programming interface
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: An application programming interface is a set of routines, protocols, and tools for building software applications. An API expresses a software component in terms of its operations, inputs, outputs, and underlying types. An API defines functionalities that are independent of their respective implementations, which allows definitions and implementations to vary without compromising each other. The API specifies how software components should interact.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: command-line interface
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A command-line interface is a means of interacting with a computer program where the user (or client) issues commands to the program in the form of successive lines of text (command lines).

SoftwareInterfaces.label: graphical user interface
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A Graphical user interface is a type of software interface that allows users to interact with electronic devices using images rather than text commands. A GUI represents the information and actions available to a user through graphical icons and visual indicators such as secondary notation, as opposed to text-based interfaces, typed command labels or text navigation.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: desktop graphical user interface
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A Desktop Graphical User interface is a Graphical User Interface which is loaded and run within the user's operating system rather than via a Web browser.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: web user interface
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A Web User interface is a Graphical User Interface which is loaded and run via a Web browser rather than within the user's operating system.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: web service
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A web service is a software interface which works as a method of communication between two electronic devices over the World Wide Web and which is provided at a particular network address. There are two major classes of Web services: REST-compliant Web services, and arbitrary (or application-specific) Web services.
definition_source: Modified from http://www.w3.org/TR/ws-arch/, accessed 6 June 2013; Modified from http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_service, accessed 6 June 2013.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: JSON web service
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A web service in which calls invoked return JSON.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: REST service
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A REST service is a Web service in which the primary purpose of the service is to manipulate XML representations of Web resources using a uniform set of "stateless" operations. RESTful APIs do not require XML-based web service protocols (SOAP and WSDL) to support their light-weight interfaces.
definition_source: Modified from http://www.w3.org/TR/ws-arch, accessed 6 June 2013, Modified from http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_service, accessed 6 June 2013.

SoftwareInterfaces.label: SOAP service
SoftwareInterfaces.definition: A SOAP service is a Web service which provides a standard, extensible, composable framework for packaging and exchanging XML messages. The service may expose an arbitrary, application-specific set of operations.
definition_source: Modified from http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOAP, accessed 6 June 2013; modified from http://www.w3.org/TR/ws-arch, accessed 6 June 2013.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: alpha
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: Alpha is a development status which is applied to software by the developer/publisher during initial development and testing. Software designated alpha is commonly unstable and prone to crashing. It may or may not be released publicly.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: beta
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: Beta is a development status which is generally applied to software by the developer/publisher once the majority of features have been implemented, but when the software may still contain bugs or cause crashes or data loss. Software designated beta is often released publicly, either on a general release or to a specific subset of users called beta testers.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Live
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: Live is a development status which is applied to software that has been designated as suitable for production environments by the developer/publisher. If a non-free product, software at this stage is available for purchase
definition_source: Allyson Lister, Jon Ison, and Modified from http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_release_life_cycle, accessed 11 June 2013.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: First release
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: The first release of a piece of software. A first release does not imply any particular levels of maturity other than is this is the first instance of this software to be considered released.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Latest release
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: The latest release of a piece of software. This does not imply any levels of maturity other than indicating this is the most recent release.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Maintained
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: Software has developers actively maintaining it (fixing bugs)

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Obsolete
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: Sofware is no longer being supplied by the developers/publishers

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Release candidate
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: A release candidate (RC) is a beta version with potential to be a final product, which is ready to release unless significant bugs emerge.

DevelopmentStatuses.label: Superseded
DevelopmentStatuses.definition: An updated version of the software is available.
